title: 材料力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Strength of Materials II
educationalGoal: The strength of materials can clarify the forces and deformations on various parts of bridges, steel towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, and living tissues and cells. Those results can be used to improve designs for safety. Therefore, it is an important subject that forms the basis of mechanical engineering. In this course, students will learn about tension & compression, torsion, and combined stress based on the content learned in “Strength of Materials I.”
advice:
This is a basic course on the strength of materials. We will cover the following topics:
1. Frame structure   2. Thermal stress and stress concentration
3. Thin-walled cylinders subjected to internal pressure
4. Torsion of shaft with circular cross section   5. Power transmission shaft
6. Stress on oblique section in the rod subjected to uniaxial tension
7. Principal stress and principal shearing stress   8. Mohr’s stress circle   9. Combined stress problem
All of these topics are based on stress, strain, Hook’s law, a beam and its supporting condition, shearing force and bending moment of a beam, and bending stress and deflection of a beam, which were learned in “Strength of Materials I.” Therefore, while reviewing the content of “Strength of Materials I” topic by topic, it is essential to make an effort to develop a bottom-up understanding by carefully considering the topics’ relationship with the content of “Strength of Materials II.”
It is important to do many exercises and review the answers, but the study of strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand by just remembering formulas and patterns. For all problems, start by understanding the basic formula and continue the attitude of answering the problem by setting appropriate boundary conditions for it. Furthermore, students should work on issues related to local companies, and deepen their understanding of the relationship between the strength of materials, society, and technology.
books:
Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu Shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reference books: Strength of Materials, Basic, Morikita Publishing Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reserved books: None specified
requiredKnowledge: Students should have a good understanding of balance of force, stress, and strain, Hook’s law, support condition of a beam, and shearing force and bending moment of a beam, and bending stress and deflection of a beam learned in “Strength of Materials I.” In addition, it is necessary to fully understand differential and integral calculation methods.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the frame structure, thermal stress, thin-walled cylinders and stress concentration.
Be able to determine torsional stress.
Be able to determine the diameter of a transmission shaft.
Be able to determine the stress in the oblique cross section of a bar subjected to uniaxial tension.
Be able to explain the principal stress and principal shearing stress, and to draw a Mohr's stress circle.
Be able to explain the relationship between strength of materials, society, and technology.

achievementLevels.ideal:
1. Design safe structures in frame structures, thermal stress problems, a thin-walled cylinder subject to internal pressure.
2. Calculate the torsional stress and twist angle of axis with circular cross section and achieve a safe design.
3. Calculate the combined stress, principal stress, and principal shearing stress and obtain them using Mohr's stress circle.
4. Understand in depth the relationship between strength of materials, society, and technology.
achievementLevels.standard:
1. Calculate stresses in a frame structure and a thin-walled cylinder subjected to internal pressure, and in a thermal stress problem.
2. Calculate the torsional stress and twist angle of an axis with circular section.
3. Calculate the principal stress and principal shearing stress and understand Mohr's stress circle.
4. Understand the relationship between strength of materials, society, and technology.
